name: SurveySparrow
summary: Conversational surveys and NPS with a polished respondent experience. Response limits on the lower tiers and a contact-sales wall on API and higher volume make budgeting fiddly, and there is no true monthly billing.
best_for: teams that want engaging, conversational surveys and NPS with a polished respondent experience
skip_if: you just need a quick, occasional form — a free tool like Google Forms or Tally covers it without a subscription
honest_knock: The conversational-survey UX is the draw, but response limits on lower tiers and the 'contact sales' wall on advanced features (API, higher volume) make budgeting fiddly — and there's no true monthly billing.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes:
(re-verified 20 September 2026 from a US exit in New York; the euro ladder was read 14 September 2026 from Europe) SurveySparrow bills quarterly or yearly — there is no monthly option — and the two differ far more than the wording suggests. On yearly billing the survey line runs Basic $19, Starter $39 and Business $79 a month, above a forever-free plan (75 responses a quarter, 3 active surveys, 10 questions each) and below a custom-priced Enterprise tier. On quarterly billing those same three plans are $39, $59 and $149 a month — roughly double — and they carry fewer responses a year rather than more: Basic goes from 2,500 a year to 600 a quarter, Starter from 15,000 to 3,600, while Business's 9,000 a quarter matches its 36,000. Users are 1, 1 and 3 respectively, with extra users $49 each a month.

The currency question is settled. Read from New York the page shows the identical digits with a dollar sign, so a European is quoted €19/€39/€79 where an American is quoted $19/$39/$79. That is the same number rather than a conversion, which makes the euro ladder the dearer of the two in real terms. There are separate product lines for CX, brand, research, documents and 360 assessment, each with its own ladder. Discounts: yearly saves up to 40%, students and education 50%, nonprofits 15%, and a startup programme offers $2,000 of credit for $500.
